svg.aria-label: Diagram: the AWS Lambda Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter captures the step-by-step history of durable executions and sends it to 13 built-in destinations. What it sends includes execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors, so the export carries the business payload rather than metadata about it. Redaction of sensitive fields and a sampling rate are both described as things the customer can configure, and the announcement does not state what either does if left unconfigured. A companion Model Context Protocol server lets AI agents query the exported telemetry in natural language, with AWS giving the example of a business analyst finding all transactions for a specific customer.
svg.title: It exports the payload, and both controls over it are things you configure
svg.text: Step input and output is the payload, not metadata about it.
Lambda Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter — free, all Regions that support durable functions.
THE EXECUTION — up to one year long
“checkpoints to track progress and automatically
recover … through replay”
steps business logic, retries, progress
waits “suspend … without incurring compute charges”
WHAT LEAVES — the sentence to read twice
“execution status, operation timing,
step input and output, and errors”
For an order workflow that is the order. For a loan
approval it is the application.
13 built-in destinations — and the payload inherits each one’s access model
CloudWatch Logs · S3 for Athena · DynamoDB · Aurora · OpenSearch Service · and others
A bucket policy now governs what a step received. Choosing the destination is a data-classification decision.
Both controls are described as things you can do
“You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume.”
The announcement does not state what either does if left unconfigured, and the exporter’s own reference is on a
client-rendered site this post could not read — so treat the defaults as unknown and settle them first.
The MCP server, and the example that describes the data precisely
“an on-call engineer can ask an AI agent to list recent failed executions” — that is observability.
“a business analyst can find all transactions for a specific customer” — that is a customer data lookup.
Export first; add the MCP server when you have decided who may ask.
The three install steps are separable, and natural-language access to step input and output is a different access
surface from reading a log file.
The exporter is free. The destinations bill normally, and the unit of data is the step, not the execution.
